samples.summary: A single non-public image `src` now aborts the whole export instead of the image failing/being skipped
samples.evidence: `createImageFetcher` calls `assertFetchableImageUrl(resolved, opts.serverBase)` before every fetch and *throws* on a non-public host or a non-http(s)/data scheme. The throw propagates out of the exporter (`exportPdf`/`exportDocx`/`exportPptxCli`) into the command's `catch (e) { outputError(e) }`, so `docs export` / `slides export` now fail entirely — no output file — if the document contains one image whose `src` is on a private address. Deployments where the image origin differs from `--server` (self-hosted MinIO/S3 on a 10.x/192.168.x host or a different localhost port, imported docs referencing intranet images) exported successfully before this change; `sameOriginAsServer` only exempts the exact API origin including port. Before the change these fetches either succeeded or produced a per-image failure at the same place, but the class of documents that used to export and now cannot is strictly larger.

samples.summary: `seg()` guard added only to documents.ts; every other frontend API module still interpolates raw ids into request paths
samples.evidence: The new `packages/frontend/src/api/url.ts` guard is applied in `api/documents.ts` only. Grepping `${import.meta.env.VITE_BACKEND_API_URL}...${...}` shows unguarded interpolations still reaching `fetchWithAuth` at `api/folders.ts:10,24,42,64,82` (`/folders/${id}`, `/workspaces/${workspaceId}/folders`), `api/share-links.ts:60,78,89,102` (`/documents/${documentId}/share-links`, `/share-links/${id}`, `/share-links/${token}/resolve`), `api/analytics.ts:127`, `api/miro.ts:93`, `api/workspaces.ts:156`. A `..`/`/`-bearing id on any of those paths still walks the session-carrying request onto a different endpoint — the exact condition the guard was introduced to remove — so the invariant the new test in `documents.test.ts` asserts does not actually hold for the client as a whole.

samples.summary: Any upstream message beginning with `<` is silently discarded, including legitimate prose
samples.evidence: `clampUpstreamText` returns `null` for any trimmed text whose first character is `<` (`if (!trimmed || trimmed.startsWith('<')) return null;`). That is intended for HTML pages, but it also drops real backend/validator messages such as `"<empty> is not a valid range"` or a class-validator array whose first element starts with `<`. On the envelope path (`safeEnvelope`, line 165) the upstream's own `message` is then replaced by the bare `HTTP <status>`, and on the non-envelope path the detail is lost entirely — the caller ends up with strictly less information than the pre-change `HTTP <status>` plus body dump.

samples.summary: `isErrorEnvelope` accepts an empty-string `code`, which is forwarded as `{"code": ""}`
samples.evidence: `typeof (err as {code?: unknown}).code === 'string'` is true for `code: ""`. `forwardUpstreamError` then prints `{error:{code:"",...}}` and exits 1, while `outputError`'s own `errorCode` deliberately requires `code.length > 0` before trusting a code (line 44). The two paths therefore disagree about what counts as a usable code, and an agent branching on `error.code` receives an empty string rather than the documented `HTTP_ERROR` fallback.

samples.summary: `isPrivateHost` misses the trailing-dot FQDN form of loopback (`localhost.`)
samples.evidence: `LOOPBACK_HOSTS.has(host) || host.endsWith('.localhost')` does not match `localhost.` — WHATWG keeps the trailing dot in `URL.hostname` for a non-IP host, so `http://localhost./x` is classified public and fetched. (The IPv4 literal forms are fine: WHATWG's IPv4 parser strips a single trailing dot.) Also `::a9fe:a9fe` (IPv4-compatible, not `::ffff:`-mapped) is not unwrapped by `unwrapIpv4Mapped` and is treated as public.

samples.summary: `upstreamErrorJson` is called on a successful response when bytes are missing, reporting `HTTP_ERROR: HTTP 200`
samples.evidence: `if (!res.ok || !res.bytes)` funnels both failure modes into `upstreamErrorJson(res)`. When the request succeeded but `bytes` is absent, `res.status` is 200, so stderr reads `{"error":{"code":"HTTP_ERROR","message":"HTTP 200"}}` — a self-contradictory envelope for a caller branching on the status embedded in the message. The pre-change code printed `{error:{code:'HTTP_ERROR'}}` with no message, so the new message actively misinforms.

finding.summary: A single non-public image `src` now aborts the whole export instead of the image failing/being skipped

verdict.reason: The code exists as described — assertFetchableImageUrl (image-fetcher.ts:111-133) throws for non-public hosts and non-http(s)/data schemes, createImageFetcher calls it before every fetch (line 151), and the throw propagates uncaught through pdf-image-painter.ts:56-57 / docx-exporter.ts:423-435 into the command's catch (docs.ts:310). But it is not a correctness defect: (a) the condition matches its written spec exactly (docs/design/cli.md:1125-1135) and is locked by tests, including the exact-origin/different-port case (image-fetcher.test.ts:111-124); (b) the failure granularity objected to is pre-existing and deliberate — any unfetchable image already aborts the export (a 404 throws at image-fetcher.ts:153-157, test 206-218) and the pipeline explicitly refuses to silently drop images (pdf-image-painter.ts:17-20); (c) no crash, data loss, or partial file — writeBinary runs only after successful export (docs.ts:309) and the core flow works since stored srcs are server-relative (backend image.service.ts:128) and resolve to the exempt server origin (image-fetcher.ts:127). The residual complaint is that the intended SSRF policy is too strict for deployments whose image origin differs from --server, which is a security/design threat-model tradeoff, not logic or runtime correctness.

finding.summary: `seg()` guard added only to documents.ts; every other frontend API module still interpolates raw ids into request paths
finding.evidence: The new `packages/frontend/src/api/url.ts` guard is applied in `api/documents.ts` only. Grepping `${import.meta.env.VITE_BACKEND_API_URL}...${...}` shows unguarded interpolations still reaching `fetchWithAuth` at `api/folders.ts:10,24,42,64,82` (`/folders/${id}`, `/workspaces/${workspaceId}/folders`), `api/share-links.ts:60,78,89,102` (`/documents/${documentId}/share-links`, `/share-links/${id}`, `/share-links/${token}/resolve`), `api/analytics.ts:127`, `api/miro.ts:93`, `api/workspaces.ts:156`. A `..`/`/`-bearing id on any of those paths still walks the session-carrying request onto a different endpoint — the exact condition the guard was introduced to remove — so the invariant the new test in `documents.test.ts` asserts does not actually hold for the client as a whole.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: `seg()` (packages/frontend/src/api/url.ts:18) is imported in exactly one place, packages/frontend/src/api/documents.ts:5, and applied only at documents.ts:47,65,88,110,155. A repo-wide grep for `seg(` and for importers of `./url` in packages/frontend returns no other consumer. The sibling API modules interpolate ids raw into the request path: folders.ts:10,24,42,64,82; share-links.ts:60,78,89,102; analytics.ts:127; miro.ts:93; workspaces.ts:156; files.ts:22 (which encodes only the `token` query param, not `documentId`). I looked for an indirect/alternate guard and found none: `fetchWithAuth` (api/auth.ts:136-164) performs no normalization or validation of `input` and simply forwards it to `fetch` with `credentials: "include"`; there is no global fetch wrapper, no `new URL()` re-parse on these paths, and no id-shape validation helper anywhere in packages/frontend (searched isUuid/UUID regex/validateId — only a comment at document-list.tsx:1158 referencing a backend DTO). Reachability from untrusted input is concrete, not hypothetical: `/w/:workspaceId` (Layout.tsx:22-26, App.tsx routes) feeds `useParams` -> `fetchFolders(workspaceId!)` at workspace-documents.tsx:14,20 -> folders.ts:10, and the `folder` query param (workspace-documents.tsx:16) flows the same way; router-decoded values carrying `/` or `..` walk the session-carrying request onto a different endpoint. Under the Correctness rubric's explicit instruction to enumerate other call sites of a new guard and report paths that reach the protected operation without it, this is a real, blocking gap; no counterexample exists.
